title: `check.ts` promises that "the corpus migration repays" the 263-file recall debt — the mechanism was deleted before #5334 merged
body:
Filed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution PM seat (#5748, PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`) as the immediately-actionable follow-up promised when **#5329** was closed as superseded. Unassigned; grading and `domain:*` are the triage seat's.

## The defect

`packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts` carries a comment stating that **"the corpus migration repays"** the recall debt — the files the D-arm skips because they have a root `type` and no ObjectUI schema marker.

There is no such migration, and there cannot be one: the maintainer's **2026-08-20 ruling (verbatim C)** superseded the `$schema` half of the 2026-08-19 ruling, and PR **#5334 deleted `OBJECTUI_SCHEMA_URL` and `pointsAtObjectUi()` before merge**. The same file elsewhere states, correctly, that there is deliberately no `$schema` arm and no ObjectUI `$schema` URL exists to declare.

So the file **contradicts itself**: one comment promises a repayment mechanism that another part of the same file records as deliberately absent.

## Why it is worth its own card

This is not cosmetic — the false comment already cost a full dispatch round. It is part of what made **#5329** look actionable: a card was written, claimed, and worked to the point of a full corpus re-measurement and a paired ablation before the dev established that the marker it was told to stamp does not exist. The measured result was that a 429-file sweep is a **no-op** on the acceptance criterion:

| leg | injected into a currently-skipped real file | D-arm skipped |
|---|---|---:|
| A | `"$schema": "https://objectui.org/schema/v1/schema.json"` | **309** — unmoved |
| B (positive control) | `"className": ""` | **308** — moved by 1 |

The comment is the last thing in the tree still pointing at that dead route, so the next agent to read `check.ts` can re-derive the same false card.

## Scope

Correct the comment to say what is actually true: the recall debt exists, the `$schema` route was ruled against, and the arm can be added later — #5334 records that host-based matching means adding it then would **not invalidate a single file**, which is why waiting costs nothing.

⛔ Do **not** add a `$schema` arm, mint a URL, or widen `OBJECTUI_STRUCTURAL_KEYS`. Those are, respectively, a closed maintainer ruling, a closed maintainer ruling, and a separate card needing per-key foreign-retention measurement (#5334 measured `label` as held out **by name** precisely because admitting `BaseSchema`-adjacent naming keys drives foreign retention from 0 files toward all 46).

⛔ Do not "fix" the debt by changing the corpus. That is the prohibition #5329 died on.

## Verification

Prose-only, so state the limit honestly: no gate catches a false comment and none will keep the corrected one true.

What can be checked, and should be, is that the corrected comment matches the code **in the same file** — quote the merged code that removed `OBJECTUI_SCHEMA_URL` / `pointsAtObjectUi()` and the existing comment that already says there is no `$schema` arm, and show the new text agrees with both. Re-measure the current D-arm count and cite it rather than reusing 309 (it was 304 in #5329's stamped table and 309 five days later — the number moves).

Run the repo's gates per the diff; a comment change in a `src/` file of a released package may owe a changeset — follow `check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s verdict rather than assuming.

## Related

- **#5329** — closed as superseded; carries the full measurement and the four-option analysis
- **#5334** — the merged PR that deleted the URL and the predicate
- **#5127** — the Option B this was the producer-side half of
- **#5392** — the `@object-ui/types` generated-JSON-Schema decision, which #5334 names as the soundest trigger for adding a `$schema` arm later
- the recall-debt tracking card filed alongside this one
